A2.evidence: result.json: loads_clean=false, survives_play=false, n_errors=3473, all 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)'. bugs.text: drawTitle calls drawSprite('boss') and drawSprite('goei'), but SPR only defines bossA/bossB and goeiA/goeiB, so drawSprite throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)' on every frame of the title screen (3473 console errors in the play-test). The enemy score table, 'PRESS ENTER TO START' and the controls line never render; the player is not told how to start. Play itself continues because the next frame is queued before the throw (line 786).

start=10-r.cols right-aligns each formation row instead of centring it ((10-cols)/2): the four bosses sit at x=142..202 at the top right and the goei rows at 62..202, visible in 4-play-015s.png and 4-play-060s.png.

Escorts are started with a negative t and held at their own slot, then on the first frame with t>=0 they are placed at pathPos(path,0), the leader's starting point, so they teleport across the formation instead of peeling off from their own slot.

Stage badges use one identical flag sprite and draw round(stage/denomination) copies, so denominations cannot be told apart and the count is wrong from stage 5 on (stage 7 = 1 flag, 8 = 2 flags, 10 = 1 flag).
A full-health Boss Galaga that rams the player only loses one hp and survives; the spec says the rammed enemy is destroyed.

The freed fighter steers towards the player at 1.2 px/frame while the player moves at 2.2 px/frame; if the player keeps moving it can miss the dock window, fly off the bottom and be lost (G.freed=null).
A boss shot while projecting its tractor beam scores 800 although it has no escorts (spec: 400 for a boss diving alone).
Dual fighter may have up to four player shots on screen (refuses only when length>2 before pushing two).

summary: A compact, well-organised file: one state object, a fixed-timestep loop, separate update and render passes, bezier entry and dive paths, a real tractor beam with capture, rescue, dual fighter and hostile captive, challenge stages with wave bonuses, a results screen and a full set of synthesized sounds. In play it feels like Galaga: curved group entries, a swaying and breathing formation, aimed diver fire, two-hit bosses that turn purple, READY respawns. It is let down by careless mistakes: the title screen references sprite names that do not exist and throws sixty times a second, so the score table and the start prompt never appear and the console is flooded; the formation is right-aligned instead of centred; escorts teleport to the leader's position; stage badges are a rounded count of identical flags. None of these stops play, but the title-screen crash alone violates the no-console-errors requirement.
